newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: France's Millon calls for quick UN action on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France's Millon calls for quick UN action on Zaire.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon called on Thursday for the United Nations Security Council to take immediate action on the crisis in eastern Zaire, where heavy fighting is threatening refugee relief operations.
"Drama doesn't wait," he told a European peace academy in Geneva. France wants a clear reaction on the part of the United Nations. It should be without delay."

Asked at a news conference whether France was prepared to provide troops to intervene in the conflict, Millon said that France did not want to be put in the "same position" as two years ago in Rwanda.
France, a military and political ally of Rwanda's former extremist Hutu regime, sent troops in 1994 to set up a safe haven in southwest Rwanda for people displaced during its genocidal civil war.

Many members of the former Rwandan government who organised the ethnic slaughter took shelter in the French-protected zone before fleeing into neighbouring Zaire. Rwanda has slipped out of France's sphere of influence in Africa since Tutsis, many of them English speakers, swept to power.
"We must draw lessons from history...France does not want to be put in this same situation," Millon said.
